catapult.title: Efficient 3-Step Workflow: predict → trace → simulate
catapult.principle: The fastest path to success is: (1) predict_first_contact to confirm the red ball hits the catapult arm (gray_platform), (2) trace_green_ball to check whether the green ball's final position overlaps the basket region, (3) simulate_action only when both prior checks pass. Skipping steps wastes iterations on guaranteed failures.
catapult.example: predict_first_contact(x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4) → confirms arm hit → trace_green_ball shows end near (4.39, -2.42) → simulate succeeds.

catapult.title: Verify Green Ball Reaches Basket X Range via trace_green_ball
catapult.principle: Before running simulate_action, always call trace_green_ball to check whether the green ball's final x-position falls within the basket's x range (~3.0–4.5). If the end x is outside this range, adjust placement before simulating. The y-position at rest should also be checked — basket height varies by seed but is typically y ≈ -2.4 to -3.1.
catapult.when_to_apply: After predict_first_contact confirms arm contact, before simulate_action.
catapult.example: trace_green_ball(x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4) → end=(4.39, -2.42) → within basket range → safe to simulate.

catapult.title: r=1.4 is the Optimal Launch Radius
catapult.principle: A radius of 1.4 consistently delivers sufficient impulse to the catapult arm to launch the green ball into the basket across multiple seed geometries. Smaller radii (r<1.0) produce insufficient energy; larger radii (r=2.0) can over-rotate the arm or produce unwanted trajectories.
catapult.when_to_apply: Default first choice for any catapult strike attempt.
catapult.example: r=1.4 succeeded in Seeds 12 and 13 with different pivot positions.

catapult.title: Canonical Default Placement: x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4
catapult.principle: When the pivot (gray_ball) is near x≈-0.93, placing the red ball at x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4 reliably strikes the catapult arm just right of the pivot and produces a successful green ball arc into the basket. This should be the first placement attempted in any new seed.
catapult.when_to_apply: As the very first placement attempt; if predict_first_contact returns placement_valid=True, proceed directly to trace_green_ball.
catapult.example: Seed 12: pivot at x=-0.93, x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4 → green lands at (4.39, -2.42) → SUCCESS.

catapult.title: Adaptive X Fallback When Canonical Placement is Invalid
catapult.principle: If x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4 is invalid (object overlap), the scene geometry has shifted. Read the pivot (gray_ball) x-position from describe_scene_geometry, then try x = pivot_x + 0.7, y=1.0, r=1.4. This maintains the 'right of pivot' strike geometry while avoiding overlap with shifted objects.
catapult.when_to_apply: When predict_first_contact returns placement_valid=False for the canonical x=0.65 placement.
catapult.example: Seed 13: pivot at x=-0.97, canonical x=0.65 invalid → tried x=-0.3 (pivot_x + 0.67), y=1.0, r=1.4 → arm hit confirmed → green lands at (3.40, -3.02) near blue at (3.50, -3.01) → SUCCESS.

catapult.title: x>0.8 on Arm Dramatically Reduces or Reverses Green Ball Range
catapult.principle: Striking the catapult arm at x>0.8 (absolute) produces a contact point too close to or past the pivot, reducing the lever effect and often sending the green ball the wrong direction or not far enough. Stay within x=0.60–0.75 or the pivot-relative equivalent.
catapult.when_to_apply: When selecting red ball x-position for any catapult strike.
catapult.example: x=0.8 with small radius produced green ending at x<0 or floor level in Seed 14.

catapult.title: Iteratively Fine-Tune X Position for Range (Within Validated Y)
catapult.principle: The green ball's landing x is sensitive to the red ball's x position on the arm. Once a valid y and r are established, small x adjustments (±0.05–0.1) can shift the landing zone by 0.5–1.0 units. Use trace_green_ball to bracket the target before simulating.
catapult.when_to_apply: When the canonical placement produces a green ball end-x that is close but not overlapping the basket x-range.
catapult.example: Shifting x from 0.65 to 0.70 can move green ball landing from x=4.4 to x=4.0.

catapult.description: Agent persists with catapult strikes for many steps without verifying that the green ball ever reaches basket HEIGHT (y≈-2.5 to -3.1) during its arc — not just basket x-range.
catapult.why_it_happens: trace_green_ball reports end x and y, but agents focus only on whether x is in range, ignoring that the ball may settle on the floor (y≈-4.8) far below the basket.
catapult.how_to_avoid: After trace_green_ball, check BOTH end-x (should be 3.0–4.5) AND end-y (should be ≈ -2.4 to -3.2, not -4.5 or lower). If y is at floor level, the placement strategy needs a fundamental change, not fine-tuning.

catapult.description: Agent binary-searches the y drop-height parameter assuming a finer value will produce the needed trajectory, without recognizing a fundamental geometry mismatch.
catapult.why_it_happens: Y controls drop speed and thus arm impulse, but once the scene geometry places green ball in a position where the catapult cannot reach basket height, no y value will fix this.
catapult.how_to_avoid: If three different y values all produce floor-level green ball endings, stop tuning y and instead reconsider the x position or strategy entirely. Re-read scene geometry to check if pivot/arm position has fundamentally changed.

catapult.description: Agent attempts placements in the basket/ledge region (x≈2.5–3.5) that are consistently INVALID due to object overlap.
catapult.why_it_happens: The basket and blue ball occupy this region; placing red ball here always triggers overlap rejection.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Never place red ball at x>2.0 in the catapult level. Valid arm-strike placements are always left of the pivot or slightly right of it (x ≈ -1.5 to +1.0).

catapult.description: Agent rapidly cycles through unrelated strategies (catapult → direct green hit → basket knockback → deflector) without converging on a viable mechanism.
catapult.why_it_happens: When early attempts fail, agents abandon working partial strategies and try unrelated approaches, losing progress.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Stick to the catapult strategy (red ball drops on arm right of pivot) for at least 5 iterations with systematic x/y variation before considering alternative approaches. Use trace_green_ball results to guide adjustments, not random strategy switching.

catapult.description: Agent attempts to knock the blue ball leftward to meet the green ball without establishing where the green ball will be when blue arrives.
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents assume a moving blue ball can intercept a stationary green ball, but green ball typically settles at a fixed location before any blue ball displacement can occur.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Always establish green ball's final resting position via trace_green_ball before designing any blue-ball-knockback strategy. The two balls must converge at the same location simultaneously.
